correctness.rationale: With 2 invertible, the five gradient generators are u²,2uv,v²,2(x0u+x1v),2(x1u+x2v). Mod (u,v)² the remaining module has injective 2x2 symmetric-matrix presentation (determinant x0x2-x1² nonzero). Map u to x1 and v to -x0 gives the isomorphism M=(x0,x1)A/(Delta), using gcd(x0,x1) for the reverse kernel inclusion. Hence M has the unique prime (Delta), is torsion-free over the conic ring, and defines the theta characteristic O_{P1}(-1). The two Delta-annihilator identities and modular law prove the saturated ideal primary decomposition. Free resolution gives Hilbert series and depth for every degree; local coordinate completion gives U²+Tv². Packaged verify.py directly checks all polynomial identities and exact finite modular graded ranks; these checks are only corroborative, not extrapolations. Limits: characteristic 2, other cubics, and any independent validation.

value.rationale: The classical Perazzo cubic has a well-studied vanishing Hessian and a known reduced singular plane and distinguished conic. The exact gradient base scheme is nevertheless mathematically natural and not fixed by those set-theoretic facts: its square-zero module gives a half-canonical line bundle on the conic, a substantive embedded associated prime, all graded dimensions and the Cohen--Macaulay depth defect, linked to the Whitney-pinch stratum. It is a motivated classification of natural scheme invariants for a canonical object rather than an arbitrary example. Existing WLP results treat another ring and do not supply this information.
